Mark only one answer for each question; if you mark more than one answer you will score zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; if you find a question difficult, move on to the next one and come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the blank spaces of the question booklet.

questions.enonce_markdown: **1.** A system of numbered squares formed by vertical and horizontal lines drawn on the map represents.
questions.corrige_markdown: On a topographic map, equally spaced vertical lines (eastings) and horizontal lines (northings) form a network of numbered squares called the grid. The numbers of these lines are used to give **grid references** (four-figure or six-figure) that locate any feature. Compass direction, bearings and direction describe where something lies relative to a point, not the numbered network of squares. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **2.** A collection of symbols used to represent both natural and human features found on a map is called?
questions.corrige_markdown: Mapmakers use agreed symbols (colours, lines, small pictures) for rivers, roads, buildings, vegetation and so on. These agreed symbols are called **conventional signs** and are explained in the key (legend). The scale, the conversion of scale and the linear scale are about measuring distance, not about symbols. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**3.** When enlarging a map twice its original size, what happens to the new scale?

*Options as printed:* A) It is divided by two   B) It is multiplied by two   C) It remains the same   D) It is multiplied by 5
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take a map drawn at $1 : 50\,000$ and enlarge every length twice. One centimetre on the new map now stands for half the ground distance, so the new scale is $1 : 25\,000$. The scale as a fraction goes from $\frac{1}{50\,000}$ to $\frac{1}{25\,000}$, so the **fraction is multiplied by two** (equivalently, the denominator is divided by two). It does not stay the same, and multiplying by 5 has no basis. Because the wording "the scale is divided by two" can be read on the denominator, the question is ambiguous.

**Intended answer: B (It is multiplied by two).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **4.** An indication of industrial function on a map is:
questions.corrige_markdown: On topographic maps a factory or industrial building is labelled "Works" (or a similar word such as mill or quarry), which shows the industrial function of the place. A road shows communication, an orchard shows agriculture and a post office shows a service function. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **5.** Which colour is used to identify water body on a map?
questions.corrige_markdown: By convention, water features (rivers, lakes, the sea) are shown in **blue**. Red is used for main roads or built-up areas, green for vegetation and brown for relief (contours). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**6.** The most convincing proof to show the spherical shape of the earth is?

*Options as printed:* A) Ship visibility   B) Eclipse of the moon   C) Circumnavigation   D) Aerial photographs
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four classical proofs are listed. Ships disappearing hull first, the round shadow of the earth on the moon during an eclipse, and journeys around the world all point to a curved earth, but each is indirect. Photographs taken from high above (aircraft and, above all, satellites and spacecraft) show the curvature and the round outline of the earth directly, which is why many school texts call them the most convincing proof. The lunar eclipse is the strongest of the older arguments, so the question is open to discussion.

**Intended answer: D (Aerial photographs).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: evidence for the earth's spherical shape

questions.enonce_markdown: **7.** Which of the following is NOT an importance of Great Circles?
questions.corrige_markdown: A great circle is a circle on the globe whose plane passes through the centre of the earth. Its importance: it gives the **shortest distance** between two places on the globe, so aircraft and ships follow great-circle routes, and doing so **saves time and fuel**. Options A, B and D state these uses. Option C (calculating distance "on the map") is the odd one out: a great-circle route appears as a curve on most flat maps and its length is worked out on the globe, not by measuring a straight line on the map. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: They form the shortest distance between any two places
They are used for the calculation of distance on the map
They save time when used as air routes

questions.enonce_markdown: **8.** The season in the Northern Hemisphere when the sun is over head at the tropic of cancer:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Tropic of Cancer is at $23.5^\circ$ N. The overhead sun reaches it at the June solstice (about 21 June), which is the start of **summer** in the Northern Hemisphere. The sun is overhead at the equator in March and September (spring and autumn equinoxes) and at the Tropic of Capricorn in December (northern winter). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **9.** Identify the main inputs into the hydrological cycle.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the hydrological cycle viewed as a system, the **inputs** are what enters the system: **precipitation** (water) and **solar energy** (which drives evaporation). Infiltration and percolation are flows inside the system; condensation is a process; evaporation is an output or transfer, not an input. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **10.** An example of human interference in the hydrological cycle is?
questions.corrige_markdown: **Cloud seeding** is the deliberate spreading of chemicals such as silver iodide into clouds to make rain fall: people are directly changing a stage of the cycle (precipitation). Droughts and tsunamis are natural events, and desertification is a result of land degradation rather than a deliberate interference with the cycle. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **11.** Which of the following is characteristics of the troposphere?
questions.corrige_markdown: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere (up to about 8 km at the poles and 16 km at the equator). It is heated from the ground, so air gets colder with altitude: on average temperature falls by about $6.5^\circ$C per kilometre (the normal lapse rate). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Temperature increases with increase in height
Temperature is constant with decrease in height
Temperature is constant with increase in height
Temperature decreases with increase in height

questions.enonce_markdown: **12.** The six's thermometer provides the following information about temperature EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown: Six's thermometer records the maximum and minimum air temperature of a day. From these readings one calculates the mean daily temperature, then the mean monthly and mean annual temperatures. It is an instrument for **air** temperature, so it gives no information about the **body** temperature of a person. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **13.** The height of land above sea level refers to;
questions.corrige_markdown: **Altitude** (also called elevation) is the height of a place above mean sea level, shown on maps by contours and spot heights. Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the equator, an ocean current is a movement of sea water, and aspect is the direction a slope faces. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **14.** Which of these is a characteristic of a hot desert climate?
questions.corrige_markdown: Hot deserts lie under high pressure with descending dry air, so skies are mostly **cloudless**, with very high day temperatures and low rainfall (usually below 250 mm a year). Two main seasons and thunderstorm rain describe tropical wet-and-dry or equatorial climates, and 10 000 mm a year is far too wet (about 40 times the desert limit of 250 mm). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Rainfall accompanied by thunder and lightening

questions.enonce_markdown: **15.** A mixture of minerals and organic material that occupy the upper most layer on which plants grow is called?
questions.corrige_markdown: **Soil** is the uppermost layer of the earth's crust, a mixture of weathered mineral particles, organic matter (humus), water and air, in which plants grow. Soil composition is what the soil is made of, soil texture is the size of its particles, and the soil profile is the vertical section through its layers (horizons). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **16.** Drought can be caused by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cutting down forests reduces evapotranspiration and the moisture returned to the air, and can lower local rainfall, so **deforestation** can contribute to drought. The collapse of a dam and rapid snow melt cause floods, not drought, and urbanization is not a direct cause of drought. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **17.** The most environmental friendly way to handle waste is by
questions.corrige_markdown: **Recycling** turns used materials into new products, reduces the amount of waste to dispose of and saves raw materials and energy. Burning pollutes the air, dumping pollutes land and water, and collecting and transporting only moves the waste without treating it. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **18.** The control of world population growth and energy consumption are all strategies to reduce:
questions.corrige_markdown: Fewer people and lower energy use (especially of fossil fuels) mean less carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, so these are strategies to reduce **global warming**. Floods and geomorphological hazards (earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides) are not mainly controlled this way, and food waste is a different issue. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **19.** A natural unit area containing a community of living things interacting with each other and the physical environment best describes
questions.corrige_markdown: An **ecosystem** is a community of living organisms (plants and animals) interacting with one another and with their physical environment (soil, water, air, climate) in a given area. A food chain and a food web only show feeding links, and a trophic level is a feeding position in a chain. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **20.** A plant species found in the Tropical grassland region that stores water in it's trunk to survive dry period of the year is called?
questions.corrige_markdown: The **baobab** is a typical tree of the tropical grassland (savanna). It has a very thick, swollen trunk in which it stores water to survive the long dry season. Mahogany, iroko and camwood are hardwood trees of the equatorial rain forest. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **21.** Which rock type is formed when magma cools and solidifies within the earth's crust?
questions.corrige_markdown: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma. When the magma cools slowly **inside** the crust, large crystals grow and the rock is called intrusive or **plutonic** (for example granite). When it cools on the surface as lava it forms volcanic (extrusive) rock such as basalt. Sedimentary and metamorphic rocks form by other processes. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **22.** Which of the following is NOT a metamorphic rock?
questions.corrige_markdown: Marble (from limestone), quartzite (from sandstone) and slate (from shale or clay) are metamorphic rocks, changed by heat and pressure. **Sandstone** is a sedimentary rock made of cemented sand grains; it is the rock from which quartzite is formed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **23.** Which of the following will be considered as a well drained area?
questions.corrige_markdown: A well-drained area has a dense network of surface streams and rivers that carry rainwater away (high drainage density). An area with no surface water or very few streams has no drainage network, and hills and the absence of swamps do not by themselves describe the drainage network. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: An area with no surface water
An area with several streams and rivers
An area with very few streams and no rivers
An area with several hills and no swamps

questions.enonce_markdown: **24.** Pick out the wrong statement about earthquakes
questions.corrige_markdown: Earthquakes destroy buildings, break roads and water and gas pipes, and can destroy vegetation (for example through landslides). **Loss of nationality** is a legal matter that has nothing to do with earthquakes, so it is the wrong statement. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: It causes the collapse of buildings
Damage of roads, water and gas installation

questions.enonce_markdown: **25.** The effective management of the soil to prevent destruction include the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: Terracing, strip cultivation and cover cropping all slow down the flow of water and protect the soil from erosion. Ploughing or planting **up and down the slope** (vertical cultivation) creates furrows that act as channels for running water and increases erosion; the recommended practice is contour ploughing, across the slope. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **26.** Development that involves the improvement in the standard of living and health care.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Social development** concerns people's well-being: health care, education, housing and living standards. Economic development is about production and income, political development is about governance and institutions, and environmental development is about the natural surroundings. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **27.** Intensive farming is characterized by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Intensive farming puts a **large amount of labour and capital on a small area** (high labour input per hectare), with fertilizers and improved seeds, to obtain a high output per hectare. Large farms, low output per hectare and little fertilizer describe extensive farming. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Little or no use of fertilizer

questions.enonce_markdown:
**28.** "Rapid growth of industries, increasing investment in agriculture, improvement in transport and services", are characteristics of which stage of Rostow's model of economic growth model?

*Options as printed:* A) Stage I   B) Stage II   C) Stage III   D) Stage IV
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rostow's five stages are: I traditional society, II preconditions for take-off, III take-off, IV drive to maturity and V age of high mass consumption. Only stages I to IV are offered. Stage I has little industry and stage II is only the preparation for growth (transport, agriculture, banking). **Rapid growth of industries** with rising investment that spreads to agriculture, transport and services is the best match for **take-off (stage III)**. Stage IV also has a wider range of industries, so the key cannot be confirmed with certainty.

**Intended answer: C (Stage III).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **29.** In Von Thunen's agricultural land use model, he proposed that crops with high rates of perishability should occupy:
questions.corrige_markdown: In Von Thunen's model, crops that spoil quickly (fresh milk, vegetables, fruits) and are costly to transport must be grown **closest to the market**, in the **first zone** around the city. Zone 2 is forestry (fuel wood), then crops and ranching further out. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: 4th zone of cultivation from the city center
1st zone of cultivation from the city center
3rd zone of cultivation from the city center
2nd zone of cultivation from the city center

questions.enonce_markdown: **30.** One major challenge in adopting Climate Smart Agriculture is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Climate Smart Agriculture (practices that raise productivity, adapt to climate change and reduce emissions) is new to many farmers. The main obstacle to its adoption is **lack of knowledge and awareness** about the techniques and their benefits. Popularity and the possibility of local adaptation are advantages, not challenges, and age structure is not the major challenge. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The age structure of the population

questions.enonce_markdown: **31.** What strategy can be put in place to sustainably conserve fish resources?
questions.corrige_markdown: **Quotas** limit the quantity of fish that may be caught, so that fish can reproduce and stocks are not exhausted. Indiscriminate fishing and overfishing destroy stocks, and recycling is a waste management practice. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **32.** Which of the following is NOT a factor affecting mineral exploitation:
questions.corrige_markdown: Mining depends on the value of the mineral, the size of the deposit and its mode of occurrence (depth, seams, veins), together with transport and capital. Earning foreign exchange is a **benefit** of exploiting a mineral, not a factor that affects whether it can be exploited. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The size of the mineral deposited
A source of foreign exchange earning

questions.enonce_markdown: **33.** Energy derived from hot rocks or water beneath the earth's surface is known as
questions.corrige_markdown: **Geothermal energy** uses the heat of hot rocks and underground hot water or steam (for example in Iceland and Kenya). Tidal and wave energy come from the sea and biomass energy comes from plants and animal waste. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **34.** In order to maximize profit, a food processing industry must be located:
questions.corrige_markdown: Food processing (palm oil, sugar, fruit, fish, milk) uses raw materials that are bulky and perishable. The factory is therefore sited **near the source of raw materials** to reduce transport cost and loss from spoilage, which increases profit. Transport, market and skilled labour matter, but the raw material is the main pull for this industry; the question is open to discussion. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Near the source of raw materials
Where there is available skill labor

questions.enonce_markdown:
**35.** Which of the factors below does NOT account for the rapid economic growth of the newly Industrialised countries?

*Options as printed:* A) Providing high interest loans   B) Restriction on imports   C) Encouraging the processing of primary products   D) Investing heavily on manufacturing industries
questions.corrige_markdown:
Newly industrialised countries (for example South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore) grew by investing heavily in manufacturing, protecting new industries by limiting imports at first, and helping firms with **low** interest loans, tax relief and education. **High** interest loans would discourage investment, so they do not account for the growth. Option C (processing of primary products) is also not typical of the NICs, which moved into manufactured and technology goods, so two options can be defended and the key cannot be confirmed.

**Intended answer: A (Providing high interest loans).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **36.** Which of the following activities are classified under the secondary sector?
questions.corrige_markdown: The **secondary sector** transforms raw materials into finished goods (manufacturing and construction). Goods taken directly from natural resources belong to the primary sector (option B), agriculture, forestry and dairy are also primary (option C), and services belong to the tertiary sector (option D). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Materials produced that are change through manufacturing
Goods from the exploitation of natural resources.
Activities involved in agriculture, forestry and diary
Generally services provided in different domains

questions.enonce_markdown:
**37.** Study the information below and answer question 37:

i. It is very flexible

ii. It offers door to door services

iii. It follows a fix timetable

iv. Very expensive over short distances.

Which of the above are advantages of road transport?
questions.corrige_markdown: Road transport can go almost anywhere, so it is **very flexible (i)**, and goods and passengers can be picked up and delivered at the exact place, so it offers **door-to-door service (ii)**. A fixed timetable (iii) is a feature of trains and scheduled flights and limits flexibility, and being very expensive over short distances (iv) is not an advantage. The advantages are therefore i and ii. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **38.** The exchange of a non-tangible items like services, tourism, best describe:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Invisible trade** is the exchange of services (banking, insurance, shipping) and tourism, which cannot be seen or touched. Visible trade is the exchange of physical goods; local and inter-regional trade describe the area covered, not the type of item. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **39.** A major factor hindering the growth of tourism in the LEDCS is:
questions.corrige_markdown: In many LEDCs (less economically developed countries) roads, railways and airports are poor, so many attractive sites are hard to reach. This **inaccessibility** is a major obstacle to tourism growth, along with insecurity and lack of hotels. Food, language and climate are usually not the main obstacle (a warm climate is often an attraction). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **40.** The following are aspects of globalized economy, EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: The economic side of globalization covers the worldwide spread of agriculture (food and crop markets), of trade and of industry (transnational companies, production spread over several countries). **Cultural** globalization (spread of languages, music, fashion, food habits) is about society and not the economy, so it is the exception. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **41.** The Adolescent age group is composed of all those who fall between:
questions.corrige_markdown: Adolescence is the period between childhood and adulthood: the teenage years, from **13 to 19**. Ages 0 to 12 are childhood, and 20 years and above are adults. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **42.** The movement of people from one geographical area to another at a particular time best defines?
questions.corrige_markdown: **Migration** is the general term for the movement of people from one place to another to settle, for a shorter or longer period. International, external and internal migration are particular types: between countries (international and external) or within one country (internal). The definition given has no limit of area, so the general term fits. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **43.** The following are all examples of light manufacturing industries EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown: Light industries make small, light goods, often for consumers: food processing, textiles and light chemicals (soap, cosmetics). **Automobile manufacturing** assembles heavy goods from steel and many large parts and is a heavy industry. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **44.** Where houses are closed to each other and are out dated at the central town. This is known as?
questions.corrige_markdown: Old, overcrowded and badly maintained housing in the centre of a town is called **urban decay**. Urban sprawl is the spread of a built-up area into the countryside, urban decline is the loss of population and activity in a city, and urban hierarchy is the ranking of settlements by size and function. Option C is close in meaning, so the question is open to discussion. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**45.** Which of these is NOT a cause of pollution?

*Options as printed:* A) Increase number of houses   B) Increase number of industries   C) Creation of dormitory towns   D) Increase demand of cars by city dwellers
questions.corrige_markdown:
More industries produce smoke and effluents, more cars produce exhaust gases, and more houses produce solid waste and sewage. The **creation of dormitory towns** moves residents away from crowded city centres and so is the item least tied to pollution, but commuting from them also adds traffic, so the key is open to discussion.

**Intended answer: C (Creation of dormitory towns).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **46.** An adverse condition after a multipurpose river project is completed is?
questions.corrige_markdown: A multipurpose project (a dam) provides jobs, irrigation water and hydroelectric power (HEP), which are benefits. Flooding the valley and changing river flow upset plants and animals, which is **destabilization of the ecosystem**, an adverse (negative) effect. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**47.** The highest mountain peak in Cameroon is found within the

*Options as printed:* A) Western highland   B) Adamawa plateau   C) Coastal lowlands   D) Southern lowlands
questions.corrige_markdown:
The highest peak in Cameroon is Mount Cameroon (Fako), an active volcano of about 4 000 m. It is the southwestern end of the Cameroon Volcanic Line, which most school texts include in the **Western Highlands**, but it stands next to the coast, so other books place it in the coastal lowlands. The Adamawa plateau and the southern lowlands do not contain it. The key is therefore open to discussion.

**Intended answer: A (Western highland).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **48.** Which drainage basin has the largest watershed in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: Cameroon has four main drainage basins: the Atlantic (Sanaga, Wouri, Nyong, Ntem, Mungo, Cross River and others), the Congo (Sangha and its tributaries), the Niger (Benue) and the Chad (Logone, Chari). The **Atlantic basin** is the largest, as it covers the whole central, southern and western parts of the country. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **49.** One of the following is NOT a cause of Rural Exodus in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: Rural exodus is caused by push factors in villages (fear of witchcraft, conflicts, lack of services) and by pull factors in towns (schools, universities, jobs). **Rising prices of agricultural products** make farming more profitable, so they keep people in the countryside and are not a cause of exodus. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **50.** One of the following is a natural touristic site in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: A natural tourist site is created by nature. The **Dja forest reserve** (a rain-forest reserve in the south-east, a UNESCO World Heritage site) is natural. A museum, a lodge (a guest house) and a palace or hotel are built by people. **Answer: D.**
